item: Clause-count-free restriction lemma (Lemma 2.1, 'Restriction bound'): under a p-random restriction, a width-k CNF H satisfies |E G·H_{T,rho}| <= W(H,T,rho)·corr_b(G) for every G, with E W <= 1/(1-theta), theta = sum_{l>b} C(k,l)(2p/(1-p))^l, valid for any constant pk (b chosen large) and independent of the number of clauses
item_type: F3 (lemma; F5 flavour: change of representation of a restricted CNF into a signed mixture of narrow CNFs)
method_note: Text-level only. The Lean was NOT compiled (no local toolchain, no local Mathlib checkout). Chain traced by reading proofs; grep over OAI/Computability for reuse. WebSearch was unavailable for the whole session (account session limit); no web query returned results. Literature items below are from the analyst's own knowledge and from data/pilot/112/{family,novelty}.* and must be checked.
lean_status_why: cnf_restriction_bound (Restriction.lean:59) states Lemma 2.1 exactly: W depends only on H and the restriction, restrictionAvg p W <= 1/(1-theta) with the paper's theta, and |E G·H_restricted| <= W·corr b G for all real G. The proof follows the paper's route (violation-path expansion, marker mixture, reweighting, backward counting) in Restriction*/MarkerMixture/ReversePath* files, and the comparator target consumes it through wide_correlation_of_good_restrictions.
lean_gaps: No mathematical gap found. The comparator uses only the theta <= 1/2 corollary (restrictionAvg_cnfRestrictionCost_le_two, bound 2); the general 1/(1-theta) form is also proved (restrictionAvg_cnfRestrictionCost_le).

W is the explicit cnfRestrictionCost: a sum over violation paths, up to card V/(b+1) layers, of products of reciprocal covered-clause counts. It is computed on H.normalize, which drops tautological and true clauses as the paper does.
corr b G is a sup over narrowTests b, i.e. all Boolean functions on the live cube computable by some width-<=b CNF. This matches corr_b.
Restriction law: each coordinate is live with probability p, else fixed to each bit with probability (1-p)/2. Matches the paper.

The downstream counting lemma circuit_lower_bound_of_small_cnf_correlations is generic in f but hard-wires the omega(sqrt n) constants (k >= 3(s+1)sqrt d, correlation <= 6·2^{-4(s+1)sqrt d}). Reusing it for parity-type c·sqrt(n) bounds needs a re-parametrised copy.

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.Circuit3
lean_source.text:
structure Circuit3 (V : Type uV) where
  bottomCount : ℕ
  middleCount : ℕ
  bottom : Fin bottomCount → RawClause V
  middle : Fin middleCount → Finset (Fin bottomCount)
  top : Finset (Fin middleCount)

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.Restriction / Live
lean_source.text:
abbrev Restriction (V : Type uDepth1) := V → Option Bool
abbrev Live {V : Type uDepth2} (σ : Restriction V) := {v : V // σ v = none}

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.restrictionAvg
lean_source.text:
def restrictionCoordinateWeight (p : ℝ) : Option Bool → ℝ
  | none => p
  | some _ => (1 - p) / 2

def restrictionWeight {V : Type uDepth11} [Fintype V] (p : ℝ) (σ : Restriction V) : ℝ :=
  ∏ v, restrictionCoordinateWeight p (σ v)

def restrictionAvg {V : Type uDepth12} [Fintype V] (p : ℝ)
    (F : Restriction V → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ σ, restrictionWeight p σ * F σ

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.corr
OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.pathWeight / pathCost / restrictionCost
OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.restrictionTheta
lean_source.text:
def restrictionTheta (k b : ℕ) (p : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ l ∈ Finset.Icc (b + 1) k, (k.choose l : ℝ) * (2 * p / (1 - p)) ^ l

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.cnfRestrictionCost
lean_source.text:
def cnfRestrictionCost (H : CNF V) (b : ℕ) (σ : Restriction V) : ℝ :=
  restrictionCost (cnfIndexFamily H.normalize) b σ

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.cnf_restricted_correlation_le_cost
lean_source.text:
theorem cnf_restricted_correlation_le_cost (H : CNF V) (b : ℕ) (hb : 1 ≤ b)
    (σ : Restriction V) (G : Cube (Live σ) → ℝ) :
    |finiteAvg (fun x => G x * indicator (H.eval (fill σ x)))| ≤
      cnfRestrictionCost H b σ * corr b G :=

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.cnf_restriction_bound
lean_source.text:
theorem cnf_restriction_bound (H : CNF V) (b k : ℕ) (hb : 1 ≤ b)
    (hH : H.WidthAtMost k) (p : ℝ) (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1)
    (hθ : restrictionTheta k b p < 1) :
    ∃ W : Restriction V → ℝ,
      (∀ σ, 0 ≤ W σ) ∧
      restrictionAvg p W ≤ 1 / (1 - restrictionTheta k b p) ∧
      ∀ (σ : Restriction V) (G : Cube (Live σ) → ℝ),
        |finiteAvg (fun x => G x * indicator (H.eval (fill σ x)))| ≤ W σ * corr b G :=

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.restrictionAvg_cnfRestrictionCost_le_two
lean_source.text:
theorem restrictionAvg_cnfRestrictionCost_le_two (H : CNF V) (b k : ℕ)
    (hH : H.WidthAtMost k) (p : ℝ) (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1)
    (hθ : restrictionTheta k b p ≤ 1 / 2) :
    restrictionAvg p (cnfRestrictionCost H b) ≤ 2 :=

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.indexedCNF_restriction_expansion
lean_source.text:
theorem indexedCNF_restriction_expansion (C : I → Clause V) (b : ℕ)
    (σ : Restriction V) (x : Cube (Live σ)) :
    indicator ((indexedCNF C).eval (fill σ x)) =
      indicator ((easyBaseCNF C b σ).eval x) +
        ∑ j ∈ Finset.range ((liveSet σ).card / (b + 1)),
          (-1 : ℝ) ^ (j + 1) * pathLayer C b σ (easyBaseCNF C b σ) (j + 1) x :=

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.restrictionAvg_restrictionCost_le
lean_source.text:
theorem restrictionAvg_restrictionCost_le (C : I → Clause V) (p : ℝ)
    (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (b k : ℕ)
    (hn : ∀ i, (C i).Normalized) (hwidth : ∀ i, (C i).scope.card ≤ k)
    (hθ : reverseTheta (2 * p / (1 - p)) b k < 1) :
    restrictionAvg p (fun σ => restrictionCost C b σ) ≤
      (1 - reverseTheta (2 * p / (1 - p)) b k)⁻¹ :=

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.wide_correlation_of_good_restrictions
lean_source.text:
theorem wide_correlation_of_good_restrictions {p ε : ℝ}
    (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (hε : 0 ≤ ε)
    (b k : ℕ) (hb : 1 ≤ b) (hθ : restrictionTheta k b p ≤ 1 / 2)
    (f : Cube V → Bool)
    (hbad : restrictionAvg p (fun σ => if ¬ goodRestriction p ε b f σ then 1 else 0) ≤
      4 * ε) :
    ∀ H : CNF V, H.WidthAtMost k →
      |finiteAvg (fun x => sign (f x) * indicator (H.eval x))| ≤ 6 * ε :=

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.circuit_lower_bound_of_small_cnf_correlations
lean_source.text:
theorem circuit_lower_bound_of_small_cnf_correlations
    (d k : ℕ) (s : ℝ) (hs : 0 ≤ s) (hd : 4 ≤ d)
    (hk : 3 * (s + 1) * Real.sqrt (d : ℝ) ≤ (k : ℝ))
    (f : Cube (Fin d) → Bool)
    (hcorr : ∀ H : CNF (Fin d), H.WidthAtMost k →
      |finiteAvg (fun x : Cube (Fin d) => sign (f x) * indicator (H.eval x))| ≤
        6 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(64 * (s + 1) * Real.sqrt (d : ℝ)) / 16))
    (C : Circuit3 (Fin d)) (hC : C.Computes f) :
    (2 : ℝ) ^ (s * Real.sqrt (d : ℝ)) < (C.gateCount : ℝ) :=

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.exists_polynomial_time_language_depth_three_lower_bound
lean_source.text:
theorem exists_polynomial_time_language_depth_three_lower_bound :
    ∃ (L : List Bool → Bool) (M : FiniteMultiTapeMachine) (C a : ℕ),
      0 < C ∧ 0 < a ∧
      (∀ w : List Bool, MultiTapeHaltsIn M w (L w) (C * (w.length + 1) ^ a)) ∧
      ∀ A : ℝ, 0 < A → ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n →
        ∀ D : Circuit3 (Fin n), D.Computes (fun x => L (List.ofFn x)) →
          (2 : ℝ) ^ (A * Real.sqrt (n : ℝ)) < (D.gateCount : ℝ) :=

speedup_targets.title: Depth-3 parity lower bound 2^{Omega(sqrt n)} (Håstad 1986/89; PPZ99 sharp form)
speedup_targets.statement: Every OR-AND-OR circuit computing parity of n bits has 2^{c·sqrt n} gates for some absolute c > 0 (sharp: Theta(n^{1/4} 2^{sqrt n}), PPZ99).
speedup_targets.reference: J. Håstad, 'Almost optimal lower bounds for small depth circuits', STOC 1986 / Computational limitations of small-depth circuits (MIT Press 1987), cited as H89; Paturi-Pudlák-Zane, 'Satisfiability coding lemma', Chicago J. TCS 1999, Thm 6; HJP95 Thm 3.3.
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: Switching-lemma route: about 8-10 pages including the switching lemma. PPZ route: about 3-4 pages. No Lean formalization known (see switching_lemma_formalizations).
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: With C1 and the f-generic Lean skeleton (wide_correlation_of_good_restrictions plus a re-parametrised circuit_lower_bound_of_small_cnf_correlations), the only new ingredient is a parity-vs-narrow-CNF correlation bound corr_b(parity on m live vars) <= 2^{-Omega(m/b)}. That bound is expected true but was NOT verified here, and the paper does not state it. Taking b = O(1) and pk a small constant gives 2^{c sqrt n}. This replaces the switching lemma by C1. It would not beat the short PPZ argument, so the gain is mainly against the switching-lemma route.
speedup_targets.expected_speedup: medium vs switching-lemma route; low vs PPZ

open_problems.reference: Håstad-Jukna-Pudlák, 'Top-down lower bounds for depth-three circuits', Comput. Complexity 5 (1995), Sec. 5 Problem 2; GPPST24 Sec. 1.1; GKPRT26 (arXiv 2601.04446).
open_problems.obstruction_match: Exact match of the barrier C1 partly breaks. C1 needs pk = O(1) for a constant b. At width k ~ n^{1/2+epsilon} this forces p ~ n^{-1/2-epsilon}, so the live set m ~ n^{1/2-epsilon} is smaller than k and the slice correlation 2^{-m/16} cannot beat 2^{-k}. Letting pk grow forces b to grow, and the sparse partition then becomes tower-sized.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Either a version of C1 with E W <= 2 for pk = n^{delta} at b = n^{O(delta)}, or slices whose corr_b decays like 2^{-m·g(b)} with g growing.

top5.argument: This is the cleanest measurable device-reuse test. The statement uses only DepthThree's own Circuit3 vocabulary, the downstream skeleton (wide_correlation_of_good_restrictions) is already generic in f, and the target is a classic switching-lemma consequence. With C1 the remaining work is a parity/narrow-CNF correlation lemma plus re-parametrised counting; without it a prover must find a switching lemma or the PPZ coding lemma. The expected gain is medium against the switching route and low against PPZ, and either outcome is informative.

This is genuine reuse of C1 on new functions. C1 reduces the open question to a pseudorandomness property of random restrictions, and the Lean pipeline after the slice is f-generic. A success would be new mathematics using the device unchanged.

C1 already controls each middle CNF's correlation; only the counting step uses exact computation. A prover with C1 in its library should reach this much faster than one without, which makes it a good speedup probe with a plausible positive outcome.
